questions.evidence:
Five review cards read delivered, bias, resumes, factual, and features. The teacher asks students to focus on small qualifications around each word. A statement may be accurate only within a certain stage, period, or group, so reading the noun alone is not enough.

A message can be delivered before the reader opens it. A sample may show bias if its selection favors one part of a jar. Regular sound resumes when a special quiet period ends. A factual book aims to provide information rather than an invented story.

For features, the class lists page count, pictures, and subject as characteristics that help choose a book. They then change one reader's requirement and check the choice again. The answer may change even though none of the book cards has changed.

Each pair writes a sentence beginning only if and another beginning even though. They explain how the added words limit or contrast the main idea. The review ends when students can support a choice with the whole condition, not just one attractive detail.
